title: TNS Media Intelligence Releases March Madness Advertising Trends Report – Sports Video Group

facts.fact: According to TNS Media Intelligence, over $2.73 billion has been spent on network TV advertising during the NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament games from 2000-2006.
facts.quote: $2.73 billion has been spent on network TV advertising during the tournament games from 2000-2006

facts.fact: TNS Media Intelligence expected 2007 ad spending for the NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament to surpass $500 million, an all-time high, and a 65 to 70 percent increase in the current decade.
facts.quote: ad spending is expected to surpass $500 million in 2007 an all-time high, and a 65 to 70 percent increase in the current decade.

facts.fact: TNS Media Intelligence's senior VP of Research said only the Super Bowl commands a higher advertising rate than the NCAA Men's Basketball championship game among major televised sporting championships.
facts.quote: Among the major televised sporting championships, only the Super Bowl commands a higher advertising rate than the NCAA Men s Basketball championship game

facts.fact: On average, 83 percent of the NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament's network TV ad revenue comes from returning advertisers.
facts.quote: On average, 83 percent of the Tournament s network TV ad revenue comes from returning advertisers.

facts.fact: Over the past seven years, the top 10 advertisers in the NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament spent almost $1.1 billion to promote their brands in the games.
facts.quote: the top 10 advertisers in the Tournament have spent almost $1.1 billion to promote their brands in the games

facts.fact: The top 10 advertisers in the NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament accounted for about 40 percent of total network TV ad revenue generated by the event over the 2000-2006 period.
facts.quote: accounting for about 40 percent of total network TV ad revenue generated by the event.

facts.fact: Nearly 75 percent of all measured national TV advertising dollars spent in college basketball each year are spent in the NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament.
facts.quote: Nearly 75 percent of all measured national TV advertising dollars that are spent in college basketball each year are spent in the Tournament.

facts.fact: Regular season college basketball games account for the remaining 25 percent of national TV ad dollars, with over 300 nationally televised men's basketball games each season.
facts.quote: there are over 300 nationally televised men s basketball games each season on broadcast and cable networks.

facts.fact: College and professional football TV ad revenue is distributed with 75 to 80 percent from the regular season and 20 to 25 percent from the post-season.
facts.quote: college and professional football TV ad revenue is distributed exactly the opposite with 75 to 80 percent coming from the regular season and 20 to 25 percent from the post-season.

facts.fact: For the 2006 Tournament, CBS signed up 18 advertisers to sponsor its March Madness on Demand webcasts.
facts.quote: For the 2006 Tournament, CBS signed up 18 advertisers to sponsor these webcasts

facts.fact: CBS planned to stream all games from the first three rounds of the 2007 Tournament live over the internet at no charge to PC users with a broadband connection.
facts.quote: All games from the first three rounds of the Tournament will be streamed live over the internet, available at no charge to PC users with a broadband connection.

facts.fact: Cingular's 2006 Tournament promotion included a chance for a customer to step onto the court and make a basket for $5 million.
facts.quote: a chance to step onto the court and make a basket for $5 million.

facts.fact: The 2007 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament was scheduled to begin March 13th.
facts.quote: NCAA Men s Basketball Tournament beginning March 13th.
